sequence_description: Direct JWT login: attempt KID header injection to select an attacker-controlled key (untrusted) while keeping victim-like semantic claims; compare against a valid control login.
description: [LLM-Judge] KID header injection appears to allow an attacker JWT to authenticate as the victim (same Vault entity), indicating signature key selection/trust bypass.

evidence.llm_judge_description: KID header injection appears to allow an attacker JWT to authenticate as the victim (same Vault entity), indicating signature key selection/trust bypass.

sequence_description: Config-change + re-auth: start with trusted JWKS URL and bound_issuer; then swap JWKS URL to attacker-controlled JWKS while keeping bound_issuer constant; attempt to login with attacker-signed token that matches iss/aud/sub semantics.
description: [LLM-Judge] After swapping the configured JWKS URL, an attacker-signed JWT was accepted and mapped into the same Vault entity as the legitimate user, indicating trust-anchor substitution enables account impersonation.

evidence.llm_judge_description: After swapping the configured JWKS URL, an attacker-signed JWT was accepted and mapped into the same Vault entity as the legitimate user, indicating trust-anchor substitution enables account impersonation.

sequence_description: Config-change + re-auth: start with trusted JWKS URL and bound_issuer; then swap JWKS URL to attacker-controlled JWKS while keeping bound_issuer constant; attempt to login with attacker-signed token that matches iss/aud/sub semantics.
description: [LLM-Judge] Attacker login resulted in the same entity_id/display_name as the control user, consistent with alias collision/identity takeover risk when user identity is derived solely from a claim (sub) and a compromised/changed JWKS can mint matching claims.

evidence.llm_judge_description: Attacker login resulted in the same entity_id/display_name as the control user, consistent with alias collision/identity takeover risk when user identity is derived solely from a claim (sub) and a compromised/changed JWKS can mint matching claims.

sequence_description: Direct endpoint resign attack: same semantic claims (iss/aud) but different signing keys. Control token signed by trusted key should succeed; attacker token signed by untrusted key should be rejected.
description: [LLM-Judge] JWT auth accepted an attacker JWT signed with an untrusted key (re-signing attack), indicating signature verification/trust-anchor enforcement failure.

evidence.llm_judge_description: JWT auth accepted an attacker JWT signed with an untrusted key (re-signing attack), indicating signature verification/trust-anchor enforcement failure.

sequence_description: Config-change + re-auth: login to obtain a session token, revoke it, then attempt to use the revoked session for identity lookup and secret read (should fail).
description: [LLM-Judge] Session revocation failed with a server-side 500 error ('no namespace'), leaving the supposedly revoked session token still valid for token self-lookup.

evidence.llm_judge_description: Session revocation failed with a server-side 500 error ('no namespace'), leaving the supposedly revoked session token still valid for token self-lookup.

sequence_description: I2 anti-replay of session artifacts: obtain two JWT sessions, revoke attacker session, then attempt to keep using the revoked token for lookup-self and secret read while victim session remains valid.
description: [LLM-Judge] Admin token revocation attempt failed (HTTP 500 'no namespace'), so the anti-replay/revocation control was not actually exercised and indicates a potentially unsafe/incorrect revoke endpoint usage or namespace handling bug.

evidence.llm_judge_description: Admin token revocation attempt failed (HTTP 500 'no namespace'), so the anti-replay/revocation control was not actually exercised and indicates a potentially unsafe/incorrect revoke endpoint usage or namespace handling bug.

sequence_description: Configure JWT validation with key-A and login succeeds; rotate trust to key-B and attempt login again with a JWT signed by key-A. Re-auth must be rejected (no stale trust anchor).
description: [LLM-Judge] JWT signing-key rotation did not invalidate re-authentication with a JWT signed by the old key (stale trust anchor still accepted).

evidence.llm_judge_description: JWT signing-key rotation did not invalidate re-authentication with a JWT signed by the old key (stale trust anchor still accepted).

sequence_description: Configure JWT validation with key-A and login succeeds; rotate trust to key-B and attempt login again with a JWT signed by key-A. Re-auth must be rejected (no stale trust anchor).
description: [LLM-Judge] Second 'login' appears to have returned the exact same Vault session token and accessor as the first login, suggesting token reuse/caching across logins rather than minting a new token.

evidence.llm_judge_description: Second 'login' appears to have returned the exact same Vault session token and accessor as the first login, suggesting token reuse/caching across logins rather than minting a new token.

sequence_description: case_confusion: Two principals differ only by case in sub ('Admin' vs 'admin'). Ensure Vault does not normalize/collapse them into one entity.
description: [LLM-Judge] Case-confusable JWT subjects ('Admin' vs 'admin') were mapped to the same Vault identity entity, indicating case normalization/collision that can enable account/privilege confusion.

evidence.llm_judge_description: Case-confusable JWT subjects ('Admin' vs 'admin') were mapped to the same Vault identity entity, indicating case normalization/collision that can enable account/privilege confusion.

sequence_description: I4 empty_sub: test whether empty-string subject collapses multiple distinct principals into the same Vault entity
description: [LLM-Judge] JWT login with an empty-string identity claim (sub) triggers an internal server error (HTTP 500) instead of a clean 4xx validation failure, indicating a potential input-validation/DoS weakness.

evidence.llm_judge_description: JWT login with an empty-string identity claim (sub) triggers an internal server error (HTTP 500) instead of a clean 4xx validation failure, indicating a potential input-validation/DoS weakness.

sequence_description: I4: Misconfigured claim_mappings could map distinct principals to the same alias value (static mapping), collapsing identities
description: [LLM-Judge] Distinct JWT principals (user_A vs user_B) were mapped to the same Vault identity entity via a static/overlapping alias claim mapping, collapsing identities and enabling cross-user privilege/identity confusion.
